Q: What is a Domain Name System 'Text (TXT)' record used for?
Option2: Storing free-form text data used for verification such as Sender Policy Framework or DomainKeys Identified Mail

Q: What does Sender Policy Framework (SPF) help with?
Option2: Specifies which mail servers are allowed to send on behalf of a domain to reduce spoofing

Q: What does DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) provide?
Option2: Cryptographic signing of email headers/body so receivers can verify the message is authorized and unaltered

Q: What is Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC)?
Option1: A type of spam filter that blocks images
Option2: A policy that tells receivers how to handle messages that fail Sender Policy Framework or DomainKeys Identified Mail validation and where to send reports

Q: In Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol, what is a 'lease'?
Option1: A static entry for printers only
Option2: The time period a client may use an assigned address before renewal
Option3: A Domain Name System zone file

Q: What is a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol 'reservation'?
Option2: Permanently mapping a client’s hardware address to a specific Internet Protocol address so it always gets the same one

Q: What is a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol 'scope'?
Option2: The defined range of Internet Protocol addresses and options that the server can hand out on a subnet

Q: What is a Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN)?
Option2: A logical network that segments ports on the same switch into separate broadcast domains
Option3: A type of Wide Area Network

Q: What is a Virtual Private Network (VPN)?
Option2: An encrypted tunnel over an untrusted network that provides private connectivity

Q: An organization wants to separate voice phones and computers on the same switch for security and quality. Which configuration fits?
Option2: Virtual Local Area Network segmentation with appropriate policies
Option3: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol reservation only

Q: Emails from your domain are landing in recipients’ spam folders due to 'spoofing' concerns. Which records are most relevant to fix?
Option2: Sender Policy Framework, DomainKeys Identified Mail, and Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance in Domain Name System Text records

Q: A server must keep the same address but still use Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol. Best approach?
